A newlywed bride arrives in a turbulent Meerut household, transforming it into a picture of domestic harmony. The Hindi comedy family horror film mixes mythology and horror elements into a chaotic cinematic experience.

Comedy & Entertainment

Reviewers note that the film is neither funny nor entirely on point with its treatment of the supernatural. Story & Plot

A social-media influencer goes in search of an old, forgotten folk singer named Naseem Bano, whose claim to fame was an off-hand compliment from Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan in 1988. He wants her to sing for his Instagram feed, but she has forgotten herself until a late-night flash of memory in the hospital. Meanwhile, reviews describe a chilling folk-horror thriller and a sinister campfire tale of guilt, need, fear, and madness set in a 19th-century isolated fishing outpost.

Comedy & Entertainment

The film does not focus on humor, functioning instead as a dramatic and psychological experience rather than a comedy. Its entertainment value relies entirely on the premise, atmosphere, and the tense interactions between characters. Audiences looking for lighthearted laughs will not find them here, as the tone remains serious throughout.

Performances & Direction

Reviewers note that the actors do a capable job, with Odessa Young acting as a capable final girl whose fierceness is tempered by the hint of repressed romance. Other cast members listed include Joe Cole, Lewis Gribben, Siobhan Finneran, Francis Magee, and Rory McCann. The performances lean heavily into the psychological and emotional nature of the story.

Strengths

  • chilling folk-horror atmosphere
  • psychological and emotional depth
  • capable performances from the cast
  • steadily mounting sense of unease

Weaknesses

Reviewers mention that the film can be a frustrating experience that fumbles the ball at almost every turn and just doesn't quite come together. The final act, intended to be spooky or otherworldly, does not do an excellent job, and the overall strategy can feel fairly predictable.

Final verdict

The Damned offers a chilling folk-horror thriller experience driven by atmospherics and psychological tension rather than cheap shocks. While it suffers from a predictable strategy and a final act that fails to fully deliver, it remains worth a watch for fans of atmospheric horror.

Story & Plot

Fighting crime full-time as Spider-Man in a world that does not remember him, Peter Parker faces the pressure of seeing his old friends move on without him. This sparks a personal change that may be difficult to control, yet it is also the only thing capable of stopping a shocking new threat that is completely invisible. Years pass as he almost single-handedly cleans up the streets of New York City, even while dealing with a lingering emotional void in his heart.

Comedy & Entertainment

Spider-Man: Brand New Day delivers an exciting, emotionally powerful, and often hilarious action-adventure experience that brings classic Spidey charm to the screen. The film balances its darker internal conflicts with entertaining moments and classic character chemistry that keeps viewers engaged throughout. Reviewers note its overall fun and lively energy, making it a thrilling watch for superhero fans.

Performances & Direction

Tom Holland delivers a dense, great performance that many reviewers consider his best yet in the series, skillfully playing the inner conflict of Peter Parker alongside the external challenges of Spider-Man. His natural chemistry with Zendaya remains essential to what works in the film, anchored by their respective roles. Other notable cast members in the film include Sadie Sink, Tramell Tillman, and Jacob Batalon.

Strengths

  • Tom Holland's best performance yet
  • Heartfelt drama and classic Spidey charm
  • Strong chemistry between Tom Holland and Zendaya
  • Exciting and emotionally powerful action-adventure

Weaknesses

Despite its many strengths, the movie can feel a bit like a mixed bag that forces in certain comic book references at times. Some reviewers also note that the post-credits scene is an insult to the film's otherwise perfect ending and should have been cut or placed elsewhere. Additionally, the film's overall energy leaves it slightly under the modern-day par of the MCU for some critics.

Final verdict

Spider-Man: Brand New Day is an exciting, emotionally resonant adventure that breathes new life into the superhero genre with heartfelt drama and thrilling sequences. While it has minor pacing or structural missteps near the end, Tom Holland's stellar performance and the film's undeniable charm make it well worth seeing on the biggest screen possible. It earns a solid recommendation for fans of the web-slinger and comic book adaptations alike.
